description: Normative crosswalk from the Advisor's normalizedProfile to the prerequisite skill's question fields. The consumer is told not to ask again for a fact the Advisor already established, but the two skills name and type their facts differently, so without this table the rule cannot be implemented deterministically: two implementations reading the same handoff would disagree about which questions are already answered. Every entry states what converts, what does not, and what the consumer may claim as a result. Enforced by tests/check-prerequisite-skill.mjs.

conversionKinds.direct: The value carries over unchanged, or through a documented label-to-ID mapping.
conversionKinds.vocabulary: The value carries over but the allowed values differ and must be translated.
conversionKinds.not-convertible: The producer value cannot establish the consumer field. The consumer must still ask. Stating why is the point of the entry: a qualitative answer is not a measurement, and a partial list is not an inventory.

mappings.note: AZURE_VM was added in v2.12. A handoff still carrying ON_PREM for a source running in Azure is not wrong, only less specific, so it converts and the consumer may refine it.
Renamed, not redefined. The alias was undeclared, which is the whole defect: an implementation could read either name and neither document said they were the same fact.
Renamed, not redefined. The undeclared alias is the defect: an implementation could read either name and no document said they were the same fact.
Same fact and same type on both sides, so it carries over without translation.
Same vocabulary. tde_material_status is a separate fact and is never inferred from it: knowing a database is encrypted says nothing about whether the certificate is exportable.
Same vocabulary on both sides, so it carries over without translation.

The Advisor records what the user said about ports; the consumer records a status. Only an explicit confirmation converts to CONFIRMED. Free text that merely fails to mention a block is not a confirmation.
Renamed and re-vocabularised. An unverified upload path is unknown, never confirmed: a real session reported a backup gate as passed with the Blob path untested.

The Advisor holds a size band chosen from a menu; the consumer needs a number in gigabytes. A band cannot be turned into a measurement without inventing precision the user never gave. The consumer asks, and the band may be offered as the default range.

A qualitative statement about performance is not evidence that a baseline was captured. Treating it as one would let 'the workload is bursty' satisfy a prerequisite asking for measured log-rate and latency figures.
A list of dependencies the user happened to mention is not proof that an inventory was run. The distinction matters because the prerequisite exists to catch the dependency nobody thought of.

The Advisor's ports field is free text about specific ports. The consumer's field is a status covering the whole network path, including DNS and private endpoints. A statement about one port does not establish the path.
